newsitem.title: USA: All eyes on July jobs, prepay reports in MBS mart.
newsitem.headline: All eyes on July jobs, prepay reports in MBS mart.

text.p: Mortgage-backed securities prices were firmer late this session as market participants eagerly awaited the July employment report on Friday.
Late in the session, discount coupons were 5/32 to 6/32 firmer, while premium coupons were 7/32 to 8/32 firmer.
Traders reported that activity in MBS was lively this session with investors making both up- and down-in-coupon trades ahead of the jobs data.
According to economists surveyed by Reuters, July nonfarm payrolls are expected to rise 193,000 and the jobless rate is seen dipping to 4.9 percent from June's 5.0 percent.
"We are in a very crucial stage. Tomorrow's (payroll) number will put a number forward which can put us in another trading range," said a portfolio manager with a Midwest firm.

Participants agreed that continued declines in rates are sure to enflame prepayment concerns. The 10-year Treasury note's yield, market players, is being closely watched. The 10-year Treasury note lingered at 6.1 percent this session, but a dip below is seen prompting a wave of home owner refinancings.
A New York pass-through trader said there was "good" mortgage banker selling this session.
One buysider reported that there was talk of large selling by an investor of 7.0 percent Government National Mortgage Association coupons.
Some investors plan to retain their MBS holdings, reasoning there was a limited upside to Treasury prices.
"We thought MBS spreads were too narrow for quite a while, but they have started to widen now. There is a growing percentage of MBS that is refinanceable at these levels," said an investor.
Participants noted that implied volatilities have risen while MBS spreads to Treasuries have not widened enough.

"MBS option adjusted spreads have been widening and implied volatilities in the cap and swaption market have been moving sharply upward and it has been moving up sharply enough to warrant even wider mortgage spreads," said William Wadden, senior vice president and principal at Stein Roe & Farnham, where he manages a mortgage and asset-based portfolio totaling over $4 billion
"I am looking for further outward pressure on MBS spreads."
One pass-through trader in New York said the jobs data will set the tone for the MBS market for the coming weeks.
"If it suggests a slower economy spreads could widen 10 to 12 basis points," said one market participant.

Late in the session, Government National Mortgage Association 7.5 percent coupons were up 8/32 at 101 30/32 to offer a bond equivalent yield of 7.219. Federal National Mortgage Association 7.5 percent coupons were up 8/32 at 101 25/32 and Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp 7.5 percent coupons were up 8/32 at 101 31/32.
Meanwhile, the Treasury's 10-year note was up 8/32 at 104 15/32 to yield 6.01.
